landing.umfHeading: What is a unity molecular formula?
landing.umfRecipe: A glaze recipe says how much of each material to weigh out. The unity molecular formula, also called the Seger formula, says what those materials become in the kiln: how many molecules of each oxide there are, scaled so that the fluxes add up to one.
landing.umfGroups: Fluxes make the glaze melt, alumina stiffens the melt, and silica forms the glass. Comparing those three groups explains why one glaze is glossy and another matte, or why one runs while another stays put, and it shows how to replace a material that is no longer sold.
landing.closingText: Try the calculator now, then create an account to keep what you made.

about.title: About Glazecalc
about.lead: A free, open-source glaze chemistry calculator and notebook for potters, ceramicists and students.
about.what: Glazecalc turns a glaze recipe, the materials and how much of each you weigh out, into its unity molecular formula: the oxides the glaze is made of once fired, scaled so the fluxes add up to one. That makes recipes comparable, helps explain how a glaze behaves, and helps when a material has to be replaced.
about.alongside: Alongside the calculator it keeps your recipes, your own materials, colorants and other additives, notes and firing logs, a page of practical <advice>glaze advice</advice>, and <guides>guides</guides> for new potters, from what a glaze is to firing it safely.
about.numbersHeading: How the numbers are worked out
about.numbers: Each material is described by its chemical formula or by an oxide analysis, plus its loss on ignition: the part that burns off in the kiln, such as the carbon dioxide in whiting or the water in kaolin. Glazecalc converts each amount to moles of each oxide using standard molar masses, adds them up across the recipe, and divides by the total moles of flux. Colorants and other additives are listed with a recipe but left out of the unity formula, as is usual.
about.guide: The results are a guide, not a guarantee. Real materials vary from supplier to supplier and batch to batch, and firing matters as much as chemistry, so test every glaze. Glazes for food surfaces should be tested for leaching.
about.built: Glazecalc started in 2017 and was rebuilt in 2026. It is one small web application, and its <source>source code is on GitHub</source> under the MIT License.
about.stackBrowser: Angular 22 in the browser (standalone components and signals), with the glaze chemistry in a small shared library.
about.stackServer: A TypeScript API on Node.js 24 and Express 5, with MongoDB 9, checked by more than 350 automated tests.
about.stackHosting: Runs in Docker on Amazon Web Services, behind nginx with HTTPS from Let's Encrypt.
about.stackDeploy: Deployed by GitHub Actions: images are built and tested on every change, and deploys sign in to AWS without stored keys.
about.credits: The regions on the Stull chart come from Glazy's reading of R. T. Stull's 1912 chart, by Derek Au (Copyright (c) 2017 Derek Au, MIT License). The <notices>full notice</notices> is in the source.
about.who: Glazecalc is made by Aaron Filson. Found a problem or have an idea? <issues>Open an issue on GitHub</issues>.
about.studio: Aaron Filson's handmade pottery is at <studio>Updraft Pottery Studio</studio> in Tacoma, Washington. Have a look at the work, and order a piece if one speaks to you.
about.languages: Glazecalc is available in these languages. Each link opens this page in that language.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.short: Glazecalc keeps what it needs to run your account, and nothing more. There are no ads, no analytics and no tracking. Your data is never sold, and the only company that handles it is Amazon Web Services, which hosts the site and sends its email.
privacy.who: Glazecalc is a free, open-source, non-profit project, run by its owner, Aaron Filson, in the United States. He decides what happens to your data, so in data protection law he is its "controller".
privacy.contact: To ask about your data, or to use any of your rights, write to <mail>privacy@glazecalcapp.com</mail>. You can also <issues>open an issue on GitHub</issues>, but issues are public: never put your email address or anything personal in one. Most things about your data you can do yourself on your <account>account page</account>.
privacy.storedAccount: Your account: your email address, and your password, stored only as a one-way hash (bcrypt), never as the password itself. Your settings (such as language, region and units) and the list of materials you have on hand are kept with it. An account needs an email address, to sign in and to reset a forgotten password. When you create an account, a link is sent to the address to confirm that it is yours; until then, mail goes to it only when you ask, such as for a password reset.
privacy.storedPrices: Prices, if you give any: what you pay for each material, per kilogram, and the currency they are in, for the cost of a batch. They are business data, kept with your account and private to it: they are never part of a recipe, so nothing you share shows them. Download my data includes them, and deleting the account deletes them. A trial's prices move into your account with its records, for materials you have not priced, when both are in the same currency.
privacy.storedEmailChange: Changing your email: the date your address last changed, so that a request to turn off two-step sign-in is never taken from a new address in the 30 days after.
privacy.storedSignIn: Two-step sign-in, if you turn it on: whether it is on; the key your authenticator app shares with Glazecalc, encrypted; for each passkey, its public key (which cannot sign in on its own) with the id and details your device gives it, the name you gave it, and when it was added and last used; your recovery codes, only as a keyed one-way hash, so nobody can read them back; and, if someone enters your password but does not finish the second step, when Glazecalc last emailed you about that (at most once a day). While you sign in, between your password and the second step, the server keeps a note of the sign-in for 5 minutes, and the page holds a short token in its memory only: no new cookie, nothing in your browser's storage.
privacy.storedSaved: What you save: your recipes, materials, additives, notes, firing logs and advice, as you wrote them. Only you can see them, unless you share a recipe by link.
privacy.storedTrash: The Trash and earlier versions: what you remove from a list waits in the Trash, whole, so you can put it back; and each change you save to a record keeps the record as it was just before, so you can undo the change.
privacy.storedShares: Recipes you share by link, if you share any: which recipe, when its link was made and whether it shows the recipe's notes, with a one-way hash of the link (never the link itself). Anyone who has the link can see the recipe as it is now, with its unity formula, and its notes if you chose to show them; never your email, your account or any prices. Shared recipes are kept out of search engines, and the link never reaches the server's logs. To stop abuse, the shared recipes opened from each IP address are counted, in memory, for 15 minutes. A trial cannot share.
privacy.storedTokens: Access tokens and connected apps, if you make or approve any: for each, its name, what it may do, a one-way hash of the token (never the token itself) and its last 4 characters, and when it was made, last used, expires and was revoked.
privacy.storedActivity: What tokens and apps did: a line for each record an access token or connected app created, changed, moved to the Trash, put back or undid: when, which token or app, what it did and the record's title, cut short. Never a note's text or anything else in the record. Changes you make on the website are not listed.
privacy.storedLimits: Limits on how often: to stop guessing and runaway scripts, counts of sign-in tries, sign-ups, reset requests and trials by IP address or account, of access tokens that do not work by IP address, of requests made with access tokens, by account (120 a minute and 5,000 a day), of changes made with access tokens, by account (60 a minute and 5,000 a day), of records each access token moves to the Trash, by token, of shared recipes opened and of share links that open nothing, by IP address, and of requests to the tools for AI assistants (MCP): 60 a minute and 2,000 a day by IP address, or 300 a minute and 20,000 a day by account when an access token is used, with at most 10 substitutions or matches a minute.
privacy.storedTrial: A trial ("Try it now"): no email or password, only a made-up name such as "speckled quiet kilns". If you sign in to an account on the same browser during a trial, what you made in the trial moves into the account.
privacy.storedResets: Password reset and email links: which account asked, when, the address a link to confirm an address was sent to, and a fingerprint of each link (not the link itself).
privacy.storedLogs: Logs: the web server records each request: your IP address, the time, the page asked for and the name of your browser. The app records errors with the page they happened on, never your email address.
privacy.storedDeletions: Deleted accounts: the account's id number and when it was deleted, and nothing else, so that a restored backup cannot bring the account back.
privacy.storedMail: Email problems: if mail to your address bounces or is reported as spam, Amazon's email service puts the address on a list not to mail again, and sends the owner a notice that includes the address.
privacy.storedInbound: Mail you send to Glazecalc: mail to privacy@glazecalcapp.com and Glazecalc's other addresses is checked by Amazon for spam and viruses, kept in a private store, and forwarded to the owner's own inbox (Gmail).
privacy.basisContract: Running your account, keeping what you save, and the emails about your account are the service you asked for: the legal basis is the contract between you and Glazecalc (GDPR Article 6(1)(b)).
privacy.basisInterests: Keeping the site safe and working: the logs, the limits on how often anyone can try to sign in, the backups, the record of deleted accounts and the list of addresses not to mail. These rest on Glazecalc's legitimate interest in security, preventing abuse and not losing your work (Article 6(1)(f)). They are kept briefly and used for nothing else. You can object to them by writing to the address above.
privacy.basisNone: Nothing about you is decided automatically, there is no profiling, and nothing is used for advertising.
privacy.whereHeading: Where it is kept, and who handles it
privacy.hosting: Glazecalc runs on Amazon Web Services (AWS): the server (EC2), the backups (S3) and the email (Simple Email Service), all in the United States, in Oregon (us-west-2). AWS handles the data only on Glazecalc's behalf, under its <dpa>data processing terms</dpa>. No one else receives it.
privacy.transfer: If you live in the EU, the UK or Switzerland, your data goes to the United States. Amazon says it is certified under the <dpf>EU–US Data Privacy Framework</dpf> and its UK and Swiss extensions, and AWS's terms include the EU's Standard Contractual Clauses, which would still apply if the Framework, now challenged in court, were struck down. The owner and AWS are both in the US, and US law can require them to hand over data.
privacy.noThirdParties: Your browser loads nothing from other websites: no fonts, scripts, images or analytics from elsewhere, and the site's security settings block them. Links to GitHub and other sites are followed only when you click them.
privacy.choiceHeading: Where your account is kept, and your choice
privacy.choiceProject: Glazecalc is a free, open-source project. Accounts, and everything they hold, are kept on servers in the United States, wherever you live, as described above.
privacy.choiceNoAccount: You do not need an account to read the guides, and you can try the calculator with "Try it now", with no email address or password. A trial is kept on the same servers for 14 days.
privacy.choiceOwnCopy: Anyone can run their own copy of Glazecalc, on their own computer or server: the code is free on <source>GitHub</source>.
privacy.choiceDecision: Whether to create an account here, knowing it is kept in the United States, is your own decision.
privacy.choiceNoWarranty: Glazecalc is provided as is, without warranty. Its maintainers accept no responsibility or liability for your decision to create an account, or for where its data is held.
privacy.keptAccount: Your account and what you save: until you delete them. Accounts are not removed for being unused.
privacy.keptTrash: The Trash and earlier versions: a removed record 30 days after you removed it, or until you delete it for good or empty the Trash; earlier versions 90 days, and only the last 20 of each record (and the one from before an access token's changes) and the last 20,000 of the whole account, but never longer than the record: while it is in the Trash its versions go when it does. Both go at once when you delete your account.
privacy.keptShares: Share links: until you stop sharing the recipe, make a new link for it, move it to the Trash or delete your account. Putting the recipe back from the Trash does not share it again. Resetting your password or signing out everywhere also stops all your links; changing your password does not.
privacy.keptTokens: Access tokens and connected apps: each until 30 days after it expires (every one expires, within a year at most), or until you delete your account. A password reset or "Sign out everywhere" stops them all at once.
privacy.keptActivity: What tokens and apps did: 90 days, or until you delete your account.
privacy.keptLimits: Limits on how often: the counts are kept in the server's memory only, for 1 minute to 24 hours, and are lost when it restarts.
privacy.keptTrial: A trial: 14 days from its start, then it is deleted with everything in it, unless you create an account to keep it.
privacy.keptResets: Password reset and email links: a reset link works for 30 minutes and its record is deleted after about an hour; a link to confirm an address works, and is kept, for 24 hours.
privacy.keptSignIn: Two-step sign-in: each authenticator app, passkey and set of recovery codes until you remove it, turn two-step sign-in off or delete your account. A sign-in waiting for its second step is deleted after 5 minutes, and an app or passkey you began to add but did not finish, after at most 10.
privacy.keptBackups: Backups: encrypted copies of the database are kept 30 days, and copies of the server's disk 7 days. So a deleted account is gone from every backup within 30 days.
privacy.keptDeletions: The record of a deleted account: 37 days, just longer than any backup.
privacy.keptLogs: Logs: the web server's, 14 days. The app's and the database's own logs are limited by size (50 MB each), which on a quiet site reaches back several days. The copies of the server's disk keep logs for up to 7 days more.
privacy.keptMail: The list of addresses not to mail: until the owner removes an address, which he does each month for addresses that no longer belong to an account. The owner deletes bounce notices within 30 days.
privacy.keptInbound: Mail you send to Glazecalc: 30 days in Amazon's store, and in the owner's inbox as long as it takes to answer you. For a request about your data, a short note (when it came, what was asked and what was done) is kept for three years.
privacy.rightsIntro: You can see, correct, take and delete your data. Most of it you can do yourself on your <account>account page</account>:
privacy.rightsExport: See it and take it with you: Download my data saves everything in one file (JSON), including the names and dates of your two-step sign-in methods (never their keys or codes), and your recipes and materials as spreadsheets (CSV).
privacy.rightsCorrect: Correct it: change your settings and your records at any time. To change your email address, open the link sent to the new address; the old address, if it was confirmed, is told of the change, and every device is signed out.
privacy.rightsDelete: Delete it: Delete my account removes your account and everything you saved at once, and "Discard trial" does the same for a trial. Copies in backups are gone within 30 days.
privacy.rightsSignOut: Sign out everywhere: ends your account's sessions on every device.
privacy.rightsAsk: For anything else, such as asking for your data to be held back from use while a mistake is put right, or objecting to how it is used, write to <mail>privacy@glazecalcapp.com</mail>. It is free, and you will have an answer within a month. You will only be asked to show the account is yours, by signing in or by opening a link sent to its address, never for an ID.
privacy.rightsComplain: If you are not satisfied, you can complain to a data protection authority: in the EU, <edpb>the authority in your country</edpb>, and in the UK, the <ico>Information Commissioner's Office</ico>.
privacy.storageIntro: Glazecalc sets two cookies, the second only while you sign in with Google or GitHub, and keeps a few small values in your browser. Each is there for something you asked for: staying signed in, signing in with Google or GitHub, or remembering a choice you made. None tracks you and none is shared, so the law does not require asking first, and there is no cookie banner.
privacy.storageNote: You can clear any of these in your browser's settings at any time. Deleting your account removes the sign-in note and every setting kept here.

cookie.purpose: Keeps you signed in. It holds your sign-in token. Scripts on the page cannot read it, and your browser sends it only to Glazecalc's own server, over HTTPS, and never with a request that starts on another site.
cookie.lasts: Set when you sign in, create an account or start a trial. Until you close your browser, or for 7 days if you tick "Keep me signed in on this device"; 14 days for a trial. Signing out removes it.

session.purpose: Notes that you are signed in, to an account or a trial, so the app knows to ask the server. It holds no token or password.
session.lasts: Until you sign out or the session ends.

trial.purpose: During a trial, its name and end date, to show them.
trial.lasts: Until the trial ends, or is kept or discarded.

settings.purpose: A setting you changed on this browser, so the next page shows it straight away, before the server answers. theme and palette color the page before it appears, and language opens pages in your language.
settings.lasts: Until you change it. Signing out puts back what you chose while signed out, if anything, and removes the rest.

visitor.purpose: The language you chose, or that you closed the translation notice, while signed out, so it comes back when you sign out.
visitor.lasts: Until you clear your browser's storage or delete an account on this browser.

region.purpose: The region filter on a library list.
region.lasts: Until you set the filter back to all regions.

includeAdditives.purpose: Whether new recipes count their additives in the unity formula, as you chose last.
includeAdditives.lasts: Until you clear your browser's storage.

print.purpose: Your last choices for printing a recipe: the whole recipe, a batch or the worksheet, and the batch size.
print.lasts: Until you clear your browser's storage.

token.purpose: A sign-in token from an old version of Glazecalc. It is never written now.

readEnglish.purpose: That you chose to read a translated page in English, so the app stops moving you to your language.

reloadedFor.purpose: After a new version of the site is released, which page was reloaded and when, so a page reloads at most once a minute.

oauthCookie.purpose: Only while you sign in with Google or GitHub: it ties the provider's answer to your browser, so no one else can finish your sign-in or start one for you. Scripts on the page cannot read it.
oauthCookie.lasts: Set when you press "Continue with Google" or "Continue with GitHub", or link one on your account page. Removed when the sign-in finishes, or after 10 minutes.

privacy.children: Glazecalc is a tool for potters and is not directed at children.
privacy.changes: If this notice changes, the date at the top of the page changes too.
privacy.storedProviders: Google or GitHub, if you sign in with one: the provider's own id for you (a number or code that never changes), when you linked it and when you last signed in with it, and whether your account has a password of its own. Nothing else from the provider is kept: not your name, your picture or any key to your account there. While you sign in, the server keeps a note of the sign-in, with the email the provider says is yours when it is needed: for a new account, where it becomes your account's email, or, when a Glazecalc account already has that email, to link the provider to it once you sign in to that account. The note, and the email in it, is deleted within about 10 minutes.
privacy.providers: Signing in with Google or GitHub is your choice, and only happens when you press its button. Your browser then goes to Google or GitHub, which send Glazecalc their id for you and your email. Each is a separate company, responsible for what you share with it under its own privacy policy. No script or image from either loads on Glazecalc's pages.
privacy.keptProviders: Google or GitHub: each link until you unlink it or delete your account. A sign-in under way is deleted after 10 minutes.

assistants.title: Use Glazecalc from your AI assistant
assistants.lead: AI assistants such as Claude, GitHub Copilot, Cursor and Gemini can use Glazecalc’s calculations directly, through the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
assistants.what: With no account, an assistant can look up materials in the library, work out a recipe’s unity formula, check it against the limits for its firing, suggest substitutes for discontinued materials, remake a recipe from the materials you name, convert between cones and temperatures, and search and read the guides. Nothing it sends is saved; as for every page, the web server’s log records each request’s IP address, time and address (never what was sent), for 14 days.
assistants.mine: With an access token from your <account>account page</account>, it can also read your own recipes, materials, notebook, firing logs and the materials you have on hand. A token made to read only never changes or removes anything.
assistants.caution: The limit checks are cautions from published limits, the same as in the app, not proof that a glaze is food safe. Test-fire every glaze, and have glazes for food surfaces tested for leaching.
assistants.write: A token made to "Read and change" also lets your assistant save a recipe it worked out with you, with Glazecalc working out its unity formula, change one of your recipes or materials, add to your notebook, mark materials as on hand, and move a record to the Trash. It never deletes anything for good: whatever it moves to the Trash can be put back for 30 days, and each change keeps the record as it was, so you can undo it on the website. What each token did is kept for you, in Download my data on your account page.
assistants.writeSafely: Make a token that can change your records only for an assistant or script you trust, and ask it to say what it will change before it does. Give it the shortest time that will do (such a token lasts at most 90 days), keep a read-only token for everything else, and revoke it once the work is done. Download your data from your account page first if you want a copy as it is.
assistants.address: Give your assistant this address, using the Streamable HTTP transport:
assistants.token: To let it read your own records, make a token on your <account>account page</account> and copy it. Your assistant sends it in an Authorization header, as Bearer followed by the token. Keep it out of files you share or commit, as you would a password.
assistants.claudeCodeToken: With an access token, to read your own records too:
assistants.vscode: In .vscode/mcp.json in a folder, or your user settings. VS Code asks for the token once and keeps it hidden; leave out headers and inputs to use only the tools that need no account:
assistants.cursor: In ~/.cursor/mcp.json, or .cursor/mcp.json in a project. Leave out headers to use only the tools that need no account:
assistants.gemini: In ~/.gemini/settings.json. Leave out headers to use only the tools that need no account:
assistants.copyForToken: Copy the setup for {client}, with an access token
assistants.copyByHand: It could not be copied for you. It is selected: copy it from the box.
assistants.apps: Add a custom connector with the address above. These apps cannot send an access token yet, so they get the tools that need no account. Reaching your own records from them will come with signing in from the app.
assistants.stop: Revoke a token on your <account>account page</account> at any time. Every token stops working on the day you chose, and all of them stop at once if you reset your password or sign out everywhere.
assistants.limits: Each address can make 60 requests a minute and 2,000 a day; an account using a token, 300 a minute and 20,000 a day. Substitutions and matches are limited to 10 a minute. Changes made with tokens are limited to 60 a minute and 5,000 a day for each account, and each token can move 100 records an hour to the Trash.
